item.description: An international team of researchers, including first author Song Xing, a researcher affiliated with the Centro Nacional de Investigación sobre la Evolución Humana (CENIEH), has just published a study in the journal Nature that analyzed four fossil teeth recovered from two caves in southern China. The team has identified two possible human lineages dating to the Middle and Late Pleistocene: one with Denisovan affinities and another more primitive lineage whose evolutionary identity remains unclear. item.description: In a groundbreaking study, researchers in Chad have uncovered puncture marks on baboon skulls, suggesting that eagles may prey on these large primates. Out of five examined skulls, three displayed signs typical of eagle talon strikes. This startling discovery raises questions about baboons' vulnerability to aerial predators and encourages a reassessment of early hominin interactions with such threats, potentially reshaping our understanding of primate evolution.
